newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gold speculators taking advantage of fears - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Gold speculators taking advantage of fears - WGC.

text.p: Large investment speculative funds are taking advantage of fears in the gold market of further sales by cental banks to drive the world gold price lower, the World Gold Council (WGC) industry group said on Tuesday.

"I talk to several of the large speculators on a regular basis and there is no doubt in my mind that they nare taking advantage of the market's fear of central bank sales to bully the gold price down and make huge profits," WGC manager of gold market analyis George Milling-Stanley said in a speech to be delivered the Diggers and Dealers mine conference on Tuesday.
"That is what lies behind the current weakness in the price," Milling-Stanley said.
The speculators sell gold they did not own in order to drive down the price so that they could "buy back" their positions and take a profit, Milling-Stanley said.
Milling-Stanley said speculative activity in the over-the-counter gold market was many times greater than what was visible on the world's gold futures exchanges.
Short positions reached all-time records in the first weeks of July after an announcement by the Australian central bank that it had sold 167 tonnes of bullion over six months.
"They (short positions) certainly amount to more than twice the annual production of Australia and could be several times bigger than that," Milling-Stanley said.
Australia produces nearly 300 tonnes of gold a year.
Milling-Stanley said preliminary data suggested demand for gold during the quarter ended June 30 was shaping up to be "pretty good," offering encouragement to miners.
Supplies of gold from recycled metal was unlikely to have gone up during the June quarter, he said.
Forward gold sales by mining companies have increased only marginally in 1997, Milling-Stanley said.
